summary: Typosquat wallet-adapter drops and executes opaque binary from non-publisher host on install
details: The package is published as `sol-wallet-adapater` and its manifest description advertises a Solana Wallet Adapter, but the shipped code and README describe an unrelated browser-automation tool. On install, a postinstall script fetches an executable from https://peerbox.cloud/sd/nSXWTpGsFd4qmzNJqWYs4w, writes it to ~/.celest/bin/chrome, chmods it to 0755, and later spawns it via puppeteer-core with executablePath pointing at that file. The URL is an opaque slug on a host unrelated to Chromium, Google, or any publisher-matching CDN; there is no version pin and no hash or signature verification, so the host operator controls what bytes land on the installer's machine and are executed. The name/description mismatch with the real Solana wallet-adapter package serves as the delivery vector, causing wallet developers who mistype the package name to install this dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
